newsitem.title: USA: New York Life loses prized claims-paying rating.
newsitem.headline: New York Life loses prized claims-paying rating.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said it cut New York Life Insurance Co's top-flight claims-paying ability rating because of industrywide problems that have hurt the company's life insurance sales levels.
But New York Life remains very highly rated, reflecting its strong market position, favorable capitalization and healthy earnings performance, Standard & Poor's said.
The claims-paying ability rating, which was cut to AA-plus from AAA, is critical in the marketing and sale of a company's insurance products.
New York Life, in response to the rating downgrade, said it is financially strong and plans no changes to its strategy of diversifying into other non-life insurance businesses.
"In our view, New York Life's financial strength has never been stronger," a New York Life spokesman said.
He said New York Life has surplus in excess of $5 billion and consoldated assets of more than $78 billion.
New York Life, which will turn 152-years-old in April and has always had a top, triple A rating, diversified into the mutual fund business about 10 years ago.
New York Life operates a health insurance business.
Standard & Poor's said the downgrade reflected concern about life insurance sales levels, which have been hurt by publicity associated with improper agent conduct over the past few years.
However, New York Life has been quick to react to ensure complete compliance with internal guidelines as well as with various state insurance regulations, S&P said.
